description: The presentation's theme, slides, and settings.

markdownpoint.description: The file's format version in quotes, such as "1.0". Its major and minor numbers each have at most nine digits and no leading zero.

id.description: The presentation's id. The .md file has the same id.

save-id.description: The id of the save that last wrote the file. Each save of a presentation in a connected Dropbox account's folder writes a new one. Other saves and other tools leave it unchanged.

md-save-id.description: The .md file's `save-id` when a later save wrote only this file. Without it, the .md file's `save-id` is this file's.

theme.description: The presentation's theme key, such as "basic". The key is the name of the theme's folder in themes/. The theme's master sets the slide size and `unit-scale`.

transition.description: The transition from every slide to the next, unless the slide sets its own. Without it, slides cross-dissolve over 0.5 seconds. `cross-dissolve` fades the next slide in over the slide it leaves. `carry-over` moves each object with the same id on both slides. `push` moves both slides along its `direction`, `move-in` brings the next slide in over the one it leaves, and `reveal` moves the one it leaves off the next. `scroll` makes both slides one strip the view travels across. The slide that `scroll` leaves stays as it was, and the next slide's first click plays with the move. `wipe` uncovers the next slide behind a traveling edge. `zoom` grows the next slide in from the center. `fade-through-color` fades the slide it leaves out to its `color` and the next one in from it.

soundtrack.description: Music that plays under the whole presentation. A soundtrack starts from its beginning and plays under the slides' own media.

file.description: The music the soundtrack plays. It is an audio file in the presentation's media or generated folder.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the soundtrack plays again from the start when it ends. Without a loop, it plays once.

volume.description: How loud the soundtrack plays. The default is 1.

fade-in.description: How long the soundtrack takes to rise linearly from silence each time it starts. It is in seconds. The default is 0.

fade-out.description: How long the soundtrack takes to fall linearly to silence before the file ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used. The default is 0.

self-playing.description: With it, the presentation plays by itself. In a self-playing presentation, delays replace clicks. A slide that has steps and leaves by a scroll doesn't wait out the `slide-delay`. Steps and transitions that start by themselves keep their own timing.

slide-delay.description: How many seconds each slide stays before the next slide. MarkdownPoint sets it to 5 when it makes a presentation self-playing.

click-delay.description: How many seconds the presentation waits before each step that would wait for a click. MarkdownPoint sets it to 2 when it makes a presentation self-playing.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the presentation starts over after the last slide. Without a loop, it stops there.

countdown.description: How long the talk should take in seconds. The presenter's timer counts down from it. Without it, the talk has no set length.

image-style.description: The style that generated image objects use when they don't set one. It is text that isn't blank, has no NUL character, and isn't "none" with or without white space around it. It isn't looked up in the style library. Without it, generated image objects have no style.

background-image-style.description: The style that generated background images use when they don't set one. It is text that isn't blank, has no NUL character, and isn't "none" with or without white space around it. It isn't looked up in the style library. Without it, generated background images have no style.

swatches.description: The colors the author has saved for this presentation. Each entry is a hex color, such as "#E85D3F".

date.description: The date the date field shows. It is a valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, such as "2026-03-14". Its year is 0001 or later. When the presentation has no date, MarkdownPoint sets it to the day an author inserts the first date field.

locale.description: The presentation's language. It is a language tag, such as "sv" or "sv-SE". The language sets how the date field is written and how text is split into words for animation. Charts show their numbers with the language's decimal mark and digit grouping. The language also sets the forms of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean characters. The default is `en-US`.

additionalProperties.description: One slide's objects, look, and animation. Its text is in the .md file. A skipped slide keeps its number in the slide list, but its `slide-number` field shows nothing. MarkdownPoint exports it to PowerPoint as a hidden slide. The show and every other export skip it. The slide before a skipped slide goes on to the next shown slide with its own transition. The skipped slide's transition never plays. A link to a skipped slide does nothing.

layout.description: The key of the theme layout the slide uses.

scheme.description: The slide's color scheme. It is a scheme name. If it's left out or the theme doesn't have it, the slide uses its layout's scheme.

background.description: A slide's own background is a fill, an image, or an image on a fill. It replaces the whole background of the slide's layout. A key the background leaves out has its default. An empty background shows the scheme's `background` color.

anyOf.description: What the slide shows behind everything. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. Without it, or with `none`, the scheme's `background` color shows. A fill that isn't opaque draws over that color. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

What the slide shows behind everything. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. Without it, or with `none`, the scheme's `background` color shows. A fill that isn't opaque draws over that color. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record. A gradient is linear or radial.

fill.description: What the slide shows behind everything. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. Without it, or with `none`, the scheme's `background` color shows. A fill that isn't opaque draws over that color. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

image.description: The image over the fill. It covers the slide and is cropped as with an image's `scale-mode` `fill`. Each key of a background image is also an image object's key. A background image has no frame. Without `file`, there is no image yet. An image that waits to be generated from its prompt has no `file`.

file.description: The image's path. The file is a supported image in the presentation's media or generated folder, such as "media/photo.png".

crop.description: How far the image is zoomed, and which point stays in view.

opacity.description: How opaque the image is. The default is 1.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are.

grayscale.description: How far the colors fade to gray.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow behind the image. Without it, the image casts none. A drop shadow's keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. The shadow starts as the shape of what casts it. It grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches in canvas units.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls in the object's own axes. The offset's x is across, and its y is down. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. Because a line has no `rotation`, its offset is in the slide's axes and scales with the line's groups. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: The shadow's color. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the image. Without it, the image casts none.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated background image. It is text without NUL characters.

image-style.description: The style of a generated background image. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, or "none". It isn't looked up in the style library. With `none`, the image has no style. `none` with white space at its ends is still `none`. The default is the presentation's `background-image-style`.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated background image is made with a transparent background. The default is false.

restyle.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made. It is a copy of a library style's `name`, `prompt`, and `transparent-background`, or the author's own. It isn't looked up in the style library. Until the restyle is applied, the image shows its `file` unchanged. Once the restyle is applied, `file` is the restyled image, and `restyled-from` names the image the restyle was applied to.

restyled-from.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is an image in the presentation's media or generated folder. The background's `file` is the restyled image. Once its `restyle` is removed, the background shows this image again.

skipped.description: Whether the slide is skipped. A skipped slide stays in the presentation and keeps its number in the slide list. MarkdownPoint exports it to PowerPoint as a hidden slide. The show and every other export skip it.

transition.description: The transition from this slide to the next. `cross-dissolve` fades the next slide in over the slide it leaves. `carry-over` moves each object with the same id on both slides. `push` moves both slides along its `direction`, `move-in` brings the next slide in over the one it leaves, and `reveal` moves the one it leaves off the next. `scroll` makes both slides one strip the view travels across. The slide that `scroll` leaves stays as it was, and the next slide's first click plays with the move. `wipe` uncovers the next slide behind a traveling edge. `zoom` grows the next slide in from the center. `fade-through-color` fades the slide it leaves out to its `color` and the next one in from it.

anyOf.description: One object on a slide, a layout, or a master. Its keys depend on its type. Every chart can have any chart key, and every shape any shape key. A key that its chart type or shape kind doesn't use does nothing. A light can have only the keys its light type uses. An override needs none of the required keys because the object it changes already has them. In an override, a key set to null removes what the object inherits for that key. The key's default then shows.
The object's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

name.description: The object's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

anyOf.description: The id of the group, model, or light the object is parented to. The frames and ends of a group's members are in the slide's coordinates. A model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with its parent model or light.

parent.description: The id of the group, model, or light the object is parented to. The frames and ends of a group's members are in the slide's coordinates. A model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with its parent model or light.

anyOf.description: The object's position and size on the slide. It is in canvas units. Its x and y are from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y. A table's size comes from its contents, and an audio object's from its icon. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide. It is in canvas units.

anyOf.description: How far a flat object is turned about its `anchor-point` in degrees clockwise. A group's rotation is the angle its box is measured at. A 3D object's rotation is in the form its `rotation-mode` sets.

How far a flat object is turned about its `anchor-point` in degrees clockwise. A group's rotation is the angle its box is measured at. A 3D object's rotation is in the form its `rotation-mode` sets. A 3D object turns about its origin in its space's axes. A parented object uses its parent's axes. Any other object uses x right, y up, and z toward the viewer. Its rotation is in degrees, or a quaternion in quaternion mode. An object's own rotation in degrees needs x, y, and z. In degrees, the object turns in Cinema 4D's HPB order. It turns by the heading about y, then by the pitch about its own x, then by the bank about its own z. In three.js, that order is Euler order YXZ. With a positive z, the object turns counterclockwise on the slide. With a positive x, its top tilts toward the viewer, and with a positive y, its left side comes forward. A quaternion is glTF's with w first. A Blender quaternion (w, x, y, z) exported to glTF with +Y up is (w, x, z, −y) here. A quaternion's parts are read to six decimal places, and its length doesn't change the rotation. Between two quaternion keyframes, the object turns the shorter way around.

rotation.description: How far a flat object is turned about its `anchor-point` in degrees clockwise. A group's rotation is the angle its box is measured at. A 3D object's rotation is in the form its `rotation-mode` sets.

anyOf.description: How far the object is stretched along its own axes. It has x and y on a flat object, and x, y, and z on a model or a light. A flat object scales about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

How far the object is stretched along its own axes. It has x and y on a flat object, and x, y, and z on a model or a light. A 3D object scales about its origin. With a negative scale on an axis, the object is mirrored along it. Objects parented to a light are scaled with it. An area light's surface is scaled too. When a move between two scales of the same sign overshoots past 0, it stops at 0.

scale.description: How far the object is stretched along its own axes. It has x and y on a flat object, and x, y, and z on a model or a light.

locked.description: Whether the object is locked against selection and editing on the canvas.

visible.description: Whether the object shows on the slide. A hidden light is off, and a hidden video, web video, or audio object doesn't play. A step can't animate it on an audio object or a light.

link.description: Where a click on the object goes while presenting. A link works when it is an http:// or https:// URL with a host, a mailto: or tel: address, or slide: followed by a slide's id. A link that works has no spaces or control characters, and an http or https one has no backslash. Any other link is kept as written and does nothing. A link to a skipped slide does nothing in the show or in a PDF until the slide is shown again.

anyOf.description: The radius of the object's Gaussian blur in canvas units.

blur.description: The radius of the object's Gaussian blur in canvas units.

anyOf.description: How far in canvas units a text with a 3D `model` is in front of the slide. On a text without `model`, `z` does nothing. A model, light, camera, or shadow catcher is at its position's z.

z.description: How far in canvas units a text with a 3D `model` is in front of the slide. On a text without `model`, `z` does nothing. A model, light, camera, or shadow catcher is at its position's z.

blend-mode.description: How the object's colors combine with what is under it. Each mode except a group's `pass-through` is the CSS `mix-blend-mode` of that name. The modes are defined in Compositing and Blending Level 1.

wipe.description: A straight edge that reveals the object as its progress rises from 0 to 1.

anyOf.description: The name of the object's text style in the master's `text-styles`. No name is built in. A name the master lacks causes an `unknown-text-style` warning. The text then has no text style.

text-style.description: The name of the object's text style in the master's `text-styles`. No name is built in. A name the master lacks causes an `unknown-text-style` warning. The text then has no text style.

font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role. On a chart, the role sets every label's font. Keynote's Chart Font works the same way.

font-style.description: Whether the text's letters stand upright with `normal` or lean with `italic`. They lean only in a family with an italic face.

number-spacing.description: How wide the digits are. With `default`, each digit has its font's width. With `tabular`, all digits have the same width. Numbers then line up in columns. Word's number spacing works the same way.

kerning.description: Whether the font's kerning sets the space between letters. With `none`, it works as InDesign's Kerning 0.

anyOf.description: The font size. It is in canvas units.

font-size.description: The font size. It is in canvas units.

font-weight.description: How bold the text's letters are. 100 is thin, 200 extra light, 300 light, 400 regular, 500 medium, 600 semibold, 700 bold, 800 extra bold, and 900 black. Each character is drawn in the face that CSS Fonts Level 4's font matching chooses for the text's weight and style among the faces of the family that draws it. MarkdownPoint never makes a face bolder to make up for a weight the family lacks.

align.description: The text's horizontal alignment. Where neither the text nor its style sets one, lines align right when `text-direction` is `rtl`, and left otherwise. An explicit `left` stays left in right-to-left text. In a table, a column with no colons in the divider row uses the text style's alignment.

text-direction.description: Which way every paragraph of the text runs. With `ltr`, it runs left to right. With `rtl`, it runs right to left. Arabic and Hebrew use `rtl`. Lists, quotes, and columns start on the same side as the text.

vertical-align.description: The text's vertical alignment in its box. Text in more than one column always sits at the top.

auto-size.description: Which sides of the text box grow to fit the text. The text never shrinks. A box set to grow can't animate its size or its text's layout, even on a path. InDesign's Auto-Size works the same way.

anyOf.description: The minimum height in canvas units of a text box that grows in height. The box is as tall as its text or its `min-height`, whichever is taller. The text is placed inside the box by its vertical alignment.

min-height.description: The minimum height in canvas units of a text box that grows in height. The box is as tall as its text or its `min-height`, whichever is taller. The text is placed inside the box by its vertical alignment.

column-count.description: The number of text columns. A column is at least 0 wide.

column-gutter.description: The space between text columns. It is in canvas units.

anyOf.description: The path the text follows. It is SVG path data. The path's coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame. The text follows the path the same way as in Motion's Path layout method.

text-path.description: The path the text follows. It is SVG path data. The path's coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame. The text follows the path the same way as in Motion's Path layout method.

anyOf.description: The space in canvas units between the words and the edges of a text's frame, a table cell, or a shape's text area. A shape's text area is the box in its frame where its words go. On a rectangle or a speech bubble, it is the whole frame. A rectangle's rounded corners don't change it. On an ellipse, it is the largest rectangle that fits inside the ellipse. On a diamond, it is centered and is half as wide and half as tall as the diamond. On a triangle, it is half as wide and half as tall as the triangle. It is centered across the triangle, and its bottom edge is on the triangle's base. On a hexagon, it is a sixth of the frame in from each side. On a chevron, it runs from the point of the notch to the shoulders. On an arrow, it is the shaft and reaches into the head until the shaft's edges meet the head's sides. On a double arrow, it is the shaft and reaches into both heads the same way. On a star, it starts as the box around the inner corners. That box shrinks toward its center until no inner corner is inside it and its corners are inside the star. When the shape is flipped, its text area is mirrored with it. On a shape, `inset` places the text box inside the text area, and `padding-top` and `padding-bottom` add space inside that box. On a text, `inset` pads the words on every side, and `padding-top` and `padding-bottom` add to it above the first line and below the last. A text on a path doesn't use `inset`.

constrain-proportions.description: Whether the object's scale, or a group's size, keeps its proportions when one side changes.

anyOf.description: The point an object turns and scales about. 0.5, 0.5 is the center. A group and a text with a 3D `model` also tilt about it. It is in fractions of the box the object is drawn at. Without an `anchor-point`, an object turns and scales about its center. A text box that grows turns and scales about the point its text grows from. Leaving out `anchor-point` is the only way to get the default.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about. 0.5, 0.5 is the center.

anyOf.description: How far a group or a text with a 3D `model` tilts in depth. The object turns about axes parallel to the slide through its anchor point. Inside a tilted group, they are parallel to that group's picture. The tilt is in degrees. A group's picture is seen in perspective through a 50 mm lens from in front of its anchor point. The slide's camera doesn't change that perspective. A text's model turns in the slide's 3D space about the text's anchor point at the text's `z`. The model is seen through the slide's camera. The text's words and their links are on the turned plane. On a text without `model`, `tilt` does nothing.

tilt.description: How far a group or a text with a 3D `model` tilts in depth. The object turns about axes parallel to the slide through its anchor point. Inside a tilted group, they are parallel to that group's picture. The tilt is in degrees.

cast-shadow.description: Whether a model or a text with a 3D `model` casts shadows. On a light, whether it casts the shadows of the models and texts that cast them. On a text without `model`, `cast-shadow` does nothing.

anyOf.description: The words as a 3D model. It is an `extrusion` that MarkdownPoint builds, or a GLB `file` that a program built. Where a `file` model's `built-from` doesn't match what it would be built from now, the text draws flat until the model is built again. A text with a model can't be in a group. The fingerprint covers the text's words, the values of the fields they show, the presentation's `locale`, the family of each font role the words use and all the theme's files for that family, and the text's style and layout. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size. The model's origin is on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. For words on a path, the origin is the frame's top left. That is the path's 0 0, and the model's y points up from it. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. The text's `z` is how far the model is in front of the slide. The model's depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play any other model's. An extrusion has no Actions. Its letters are matte and lit only by the slide's lights and World. With no light and the World's intensity at 0, they draw black. The World's intensity is 0 by default.

That is the path's 0 0, and the model's y points up from it. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. The text's `z` is how far the model is in front of the slide. The model's depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play any other model's. An extrusion has no Actions. Its letters are matte and lit only by the slide's lights and World. With no light and the World's intensity at 0, they draw black. The World's intensity is 0 by default.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. A piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. `based-on` sets which. `delivery: by-paragraph` works the same way as PowerPoint's By Paragraph.

anyOf.description: Text that exits piece by piece. A piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. An exit's pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. A piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. An exit's pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's.

anyOf.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells, or in a text's frame behind its words. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. A text's words have their own color over the fill. With `none`, there is no fill. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

fill.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells, or in a text's frame behind its words. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. A text's words have their own color over the fill. With `none`, there is no fill. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

stroke-style.description: Whether the outline or the line is solid, dashed, or dotted.

anyOf.description: A description of the object that screen readers read aloud. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. On a shape or a table, the description is read before the words. On a chart, it is read in place of the labels. Without `alt`, an image whose picture matches its code is described by that code on one line. When an edit in MarkdownPoint changes an icon's own `icon` key, the edit removes the icon's `alt` too. An `alt` given in the same edit stays. A step's keyframe for `icon` leaves `alt` as it is. When an edit gives an image or a video another `file`, the edit removes the object's `alt` too. When the object inherits an `alt`, the edit sets `alt` to null in its override. `alt` stays as it is when an edit applies or removes a restyle, gives the image its `restyled-from` file, renames or moves the object's file, gives the image a copy of its file to open in an image editor, or gives a theme's image or video a file for one color scheme. When an edit removes the `file` of an object that isn't inherited, the edit removes its `alt` too. When an edit resets or removes a `file` that an override gives, the edit removes the override's `alt` too. The object then has the `alt` it inherits. An edit that removes an inherited `file`, or resets a `null` `file` alone, leaves `alt` as it is because that `alt` describes what the inherited `file` shows. None of these edits changes the `alt` of an image with `source` because its picture is made from its code. An `alt` given after the `file` in the same edit stays. A change written directly into the presentation's files leaves `alt` as it is too.

column-widths.description: The width of each of a table's columns in order. The table is as wide as its columns. Without a list, or past its end, a column is 240 times the master's `default-scale` wide.

min-row-heights.description: The minimum height of each row. A row is taller when its words need more. A row of 0, or one past the list, has no minimum and is as tall as its words. The table is as tall as its rows.

header-row.description: Whether the table's first row is styled as a header.

header-column.description: Whether the table's first column is styled as a header.

alternating-rows.description: Whether every other row is shaded.

gridlines.description: Which of the table's lines show. With `none`, no lines show. With `horizontal`, the lines between rows show with the top and bottom edges. With `all`, every line shows with all four edges.

anyOf.description: The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

file.description: The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

scale-mode.description: How an image or video fills its frame. With `fill`, it covers the frame and the rest is cropped. With `fit`, all of it shows inside the frame.

crop.description: How far the image or video is zoomed inside its frame, and which point stays in view.

flip.description: How the object's picture, glyph, or outline is mirrored along its own axes. An image's `mask`, a shape's gradients, and a shape's text aren't mirrored.

grayscale.description: How far the colors fade to gray.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are.

anyOf.description: The radius of a rectangle's, an image's, or a video's corners in canvas units. An image's or a video's corners are its frame's. A masked image's radius isn't drawn until its mask is removed.

corner-radius.description: The radius of a rectangle's, an image's, or a video's corners in canvas units. An image's or a video's corners are its frame's. A masked image's radius isn't drawn until its mask is removed.

anyOf.description: The shape the image is cut to. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the image's frame. The shape is filled by the nonzero rule.

mask.description: The shape the image is cut to. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the image's frame. The shape is filled by the nonzero rule.

decorative.description: Whether screen readers skip the object as decoration. A decorative shape's words and a decorative chart's labels are skipped too. Without `alt`, an image, video, web video, model, icon, or chart that isn't decorative causes a warning once it has something to show. A counter causes no warning because screen readers read its figure. An image whose picture matches its code causes none either.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated image is made with a transparent background.

anyOf.description: The prompt for a generated image. It is text without NUL characters.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated image. It is text without NUL characters.

anyOf.description: The style a generated image is made in. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, or "none". It isn't looked up in the style library. With `none`, the image has no style. `none` with white space at its ends is still `none`. The default is the presentation's `image-style`.

image-style.description: The style a generated image is made in. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, or "none". It isn't looked up in the style library. With `none`, the image has no style. `none` with white space at its ends is still `none`. The default is the presentation's `image-style`.

anyOf.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made. It is a copy of a library style's `name`, `prompt`, and `transparent-background`, or the author's own. It isn't looked up in the style library. Until the restyle is applied, the image shows its `file` unchanged. Once the restyle is applied, `file` is the restyled image, and `restyled-from` names the image the restyle was applied to.

restyle.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made. It is a copy of a library style's `name`, `prompt`, and `transparent-background`, or the author's own. It isn't looked up in the style library. Until the restyle is applied, the image shows its `file` unchanged. Once the restyle is applied, `file` is the restyled image, and `restyled-from` names the image the restyle was applied to.

anyOf.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is an image in the presentation's media or generated folder. The image object's `file` is the restyled image. Once its `restyle` is removed, the image object shows this image again.

restyled-from.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is an image in the presentation's media or generated folder. The image object's `file` is the restyled image. Once its `restyle` is removed, the image object shows this image again.

anyOf.description: The code an image's picture is made from. An image with `source` is never generated from a prompt. Its `prompt`, `image-style`, `transparent-background`, `restyle`, and `restyled-from` are left out as the file is read. Each causes a `generation-with-source` warning. A save doesn't remove them. A program makes the picture only when an author asks it to. The image shows its `file`, whatever its code says. The `type` names the code's language.

source.description: The code an image's picture is made from. An image with `source` is never generated from a prompt. Its `prompt`, `image-style`, `transparent-background`, `restyle`, and `restyled-from` are left out as the file is read. Each causes a `generation-with-source` warning. A save doesn't remove them. A program makes the picture only when an author asks it to. The image shows its `file`, whatever its code says. The `type` names the code's language.

anyOf.description: The fingerprint of what the image's `file` was made from. It is written as `markdownpoint/<type>/<rule>:sha256:<hex>`. It ends with the SHA-256 of a record that has the `type` and `code` of the image's `source`. A diagram's fingerprint covers the master's body font too. The record's `font` is that font's name as the master's `fonts` spells it. When MarkdownPoint ships the font and the theme has no faces of its own for it, the name has MarkdownPoint's spelling, such as Inter for INTER. The record is written according to RFC 8785's JSON Canonicalization Scheme. A reader that doesn't know the fingerprint's rule treats the picture as out of date. Without `source`, the `built-from` is left out as the file is read. It then causes a `built-from-without-source` warning.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the image's `file` was made from. It is written as `markdownpoint/<type>/<rule>:sha256:<hex>`. It ends with the SHA-256 of a record that has the `type` and `code` of the image's `source`. A diagram's fingerprint covers the master's body font too. The record's `font` is that font's name as the master's `fonts` spells it. When MarkdownPoint ships the font and the theme has no faces of its own for it, the name has MarkdownPoint's spelling, such as Inter for INTER. The record is written according to RFC 8785's JSON Canonicalization Scheme. A reader that doesn't know the fingerprint's rule treats the picture as out of date. Without `source`, the `built-from` is left out as the file is read. It then causes a `built-from-without-source` warning.

anyOf.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed from the one before. The original stays as written.

repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed from the one before. The original stays as written.

start-on.description: With `cue`, the video, audio, or web video starts at a `play` cue. With `slide`, it starts once the transition into its slide has ended, or with the step that first shows it. No `play` cue starts it then.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the video or audio plays again from the start of its `media-trim` each time it ends. Without a loop, it plays once. A video then stays on the frame where it stops.

volume.description: How loud the video or audio plays. 1 is the file's own level.

anyOf.description: How long a video's sound takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds. The video's picture doesn't fade.

audio-fade-in.description: How long a video's sound takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds. The video's picture doesn't fade.

anyOf.description: How long a video's sound takes to fall linearly to silence before the part set by `media-trim` ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

audio-fade-out.description: How long a video's sound takes to fall linearly to silence before the part set by `media-trim` ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

anyOf.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays. It is a start and an end in seconds.

media-trim.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays. It is a start and an end in seconds.

anyOf.description: The path to the image the video shows before it plays. The file is a supported image in the presentation's media or generated folder, such as "media/photo.png". Without a `poster`, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. An override that sets a video's `poster` or `poster-time` replaces both.

poster.description: The path to the image the video shows before it plays. The file is a supported image in the presentation's media or generated folder, such as "media/photo.png". Without a `poster`, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. An override that sets a video's `poster` or `poster-time` replaces both.

anyOf.description: The time of the frame the video shows before it plays when it has no `poster`. It is in seconds from the start of the video's file. The default is the start of its `media-trim`.

poster-time.description: The time of the frame the video shows before it plays when it has no `poster`. It is in seconds from the start of the video's file. The default is the start of its `media-trim`.

shape-type.description: Which shape a shape object draws. An edit that changes it drops each key the new kind doesn't use. A step that changes it drops none.

anyOf.description: How many points a star has.

point-count.description: How many points a star has.

anyOf.description: Where a speech bubble's tail ends. It is in fractions of the bubble's frame.

tail.description: Where a speech bubble's tail ends. It is in fractions of the bubble's frame.

use-as-mask.description: Whether the shape or path clips the members after it in its group to its outline.

anyOf.description: The path's outline. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame.

geometry.description: The path's outline. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame.

fill-rule.description: Which areas of a self-crossing path the fill covers. A path used as a mask clips to the same areas.

anyOf.description: The drawn part of the stroke. A trim runs from `start` to `end` along a path's or a line's stroke.

trim.description: The drawn part of the stroke. A trim runs from `start` to `end` along a path's or a line's stroke.

icon.description: The name of the Lucide 1.46.0 icon the object draws. It is the icon's own name, not an alias. A later version never drops a name.

anyOf.description: Where a line starts. The start is a point, or an object the line stays attached to. An attached end is straight out from the object's center toward its `side`. On a speech bubble or an object that isn't a shape, it meets the frame's edge. On any other shape, it meets the shape's outline.
Where a line starts. The start is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

start.description: Where a line starts. The start is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

anyOf.description: Where a line ends. The end is a point, or an object the line stays attached to. An attached end is straight out from the object's center toward its `side`. On a speech bubble or an object that isn't a shape, it meets the frame's edge. On any other shape, it meets the shape's outline.
Where a line ends. The end is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

end.description: Where a line ends. The end is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

connection.description: How a line runs between its ends. An elbow line turns at right angles halfway between its ends.

anyOf.description: How far a curved line's middle bends from straight in multiples of the distance between its ends. A positive bend goes right, seen from the start toward the end.

bend.description: How far a curved line's middle bends from straight in multiples of the distance between its ends. A positive bend goes right, seen from the start toward the end.

cap-start.description: What the start of the line shows.

cap-end.description: What the end of the line shows.

chart-type.description: Which chart the object draws. A column or a bar chart places each category's columns or bars side by side. A stacked column or bar chart stacks them. A line chart draws a line for each series, and a stacked area chart an area for each. A pie or a donut shows the first series. A counter shows the first value.

progress.description: How far the chart has grown in. A counter counts from 0 up to its value as `progress` rises.

delivery.description: How the chart's elements grow. With `by-element`, they grow one after another as `progress` rises. Without it, all grow at once.

anyOf.description: With `delivery`, how many intervals each element grows for. Without `delivery`, `spread` does nothing.

spread.description: With `delivery`, how many intervals each element grows for. Without `delivery`, `spread` does nothing.

digits.description: How a counter's digits reach each value as it grows. With `change`, each digit changes in place. With `roll`, the digits roll into place like an odometer's.

value-labels.description: Where the chart labels its values. With `none`, it shows no value labels. With `auto`, each label shows past a bar's or a column's end, above or below a point, or inside a slice, a stacked segment, or a stacked area. A counter shows its figure either way.

legend.description: Where the chart shows a legend. With `none`, there is no legend. With `top`, it runs across the top of the chart. It names a pie's or a donut's categories, or any other chart's series.

series-colors.description: The colors of the chart's series in order. Every chart but a pie, a donut, or a counter uses them. For a `null` or missing entry, the chart uses the slide's colors by the entry's place: `accent` for the first, `text` for the second, and so on in turn. Where `accent` is the same color as `text` and `muted` isn't, `muted` takes the place of `text`. Each time the two repeat, they are drawn at a lower opacity.

category-colors.description: The colors of the chart's categories in order. A pie or a donut uses one for each slice. For a `null` or missing entry, the chart uses the slide's colors by the entry's place: `accent` for the first, `text` for the second, and so on in turn. Where `accent` is the same color as `text` and `muted` isn't, `muted` takes the place of `text`. Each time the two repeat, they are drawn at a lower opacity.

leading-zero-opacity.description: The opacity of a rolling counter's unused leading zeros. They are the zeros to the left of both the counter's number and the whole digits its cell has. Without `digits: roll`, `leading-zero-opacity` does nothing.

anyOf.description: How long the audio takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds.

fade-in.description: How long the audio takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds.

anyOf.description: How long the audio takes to fall linearly to silence before the part set by `media-trim` ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

fade-out.description: How long the audio takes to fall linearly to silence before the part set by `media-trim` ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

url.description: The https address of a YouTube or Vimeo video. An override's `url` replaces the whole video. A web video's `poster` changes only with its `url`.

anyOf.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A point in the 3D space is in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A floor is level and goes on without end. Like a shadow catcher, a floor shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

position.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y.

rotation-mode.description: The form of a 3D object's rotation. Without it, the rotation is in degrees in Cinema 4D's HPB order. With `quaternion`, it is written as w, x, y, and z in its space's axes.

anyOf.description: The node of the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. It is the name of one of the model's nodes. Without it, the object moves with the whole model.

parent-node.description: The node of the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. It is the name of one of the model's nodes. Without it, the object moves with the whole model.

parent-inverse.description: The matrix that leaves the object where it was when it was parented. It has 16 numbers, column by column. Its fourth row is 0, 0, 0, and 1. Those are its 4th, 8th, 12th, and 16th numbers.

anyOf.description: The camera lens's focal length in millimeters.

focal-length.description: The camera lens's focal length in millimeters.

anyOf.description: How far in canvas units the camera's lens is shifted up. A lens shift works the same way as Cinema 4D's Film Offset Y, Maya's Vertical Film Offset, and Blender's Shift Y. The camera doesn't turn. What is straight ahead of it shows that far below the picture's middle. The default position's y is that much lower. A level camera whose position leaves out y and z then shows what is at z 0 where the slide lays it out. With a negative shift, the camera is higher and sees the floor from above. With y set, only the lens shifts. A camera with a point of interest turns just enough to show that point at the picture's middle. The default is minus a quarter of the slide's height. A level camera then shows its horizon a quarter of the way down. Write 0 for a camera at the slide's middle.

lens-shift.description: How far in canvas units the camera's lens is shifted up. A lens shift works the same way as Cinema 4D's Film Offset Y, Maya's Vertical Film Offset, and Blender's Shift Y. The camera doesn't turn. What is straight ahead of it shows that far below the picture's middle. The default position's y is that much lower. A level camera whose position leaves out y and z then shows what is at z 0 where the slide lays it out. With a negative shift, the camera is higher and sees the floor from above. With y set, only the lens shifts. A camera with a point of interest turns just enough to show that point at the picture's middle. The default is minus a quarter of the slide's height. A level camera then shows its horizon a quarter of the way down. Write 0 for a camera at the slide's middle.

anyOf.description: The camera's motion blur. The 3D layer blurs along its motion while the shutter is open. Nothing else is blurred. Only exported movies and the Agent's renders show it. A frame is a sixtieth of a second in a movie and in the Agent's renders at any `sampleRate`.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open in frames. At 0, there is no blur. It can be animated. The default is 0.5.

shutter-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the time the shutter is open. The default is `center`.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open. The drawings are then averaged. Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples work the same way. The default is 32.

motion-blur.description: The camera's motion blur. The 3D layer blurs along its motion while the shutter is open. Nothing else is blurred. Only exported movies and the Agent's renders show it. A frame is a sixtieth of a second in a movie and in the Agent's renders at any `sampleRate`.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what is near them. The default is false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other. A shadow catcher or a floor then also darkens where an object rests on it. The default is false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface in canvas units. The default is 400 times the master's `default-scale`.

render-effects.description: The slide's two render effects. One is a fast estimate of the light that bounces between surfaces. The other is a fast estimate of the World's light that is blocked where surfaces meet. Both are set on the slide's camera. Motion blur is set there too.

anyOf.description: The point the camera or a directional, spot, or area light faces. It is used in place of the rotation. It is in the position's space. The camera's or light's top stays toward the top of that space. A point in the 3D space is in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

point-of-interest.description: The point the camera or a directional, spot, or area light faces. It is used in place of the rotation. It is in the position's space. The camera's or light's top stays toward the top of that space.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object. Cinema 4D's Position constraint works the same way. Only the camera can have it. With a `spring`, the camera follows on a spring with its `response` and `damping-ratio`. The camera trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. If the spring is still moving 10 seconds after what the camera follows has stopped, the camera halts where it got to. It stops short of its target. It stays there until a click moves what it follows again. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as "look". It is unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.<id>.strength`.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of the node in the target's model that the camera follows, such as ball. The camera follows that node as the target's Action moves it. Without `target-node`, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: A list of one or more of the 3D space's axes the camera follows on, such as `["x"]`. Each axis is listed once. The axes can be in any order. The default is `x`, `y`, and `z`.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera follows the target at an offset. The offset is the camera's own offset from the slide's center at z 0, and it is added to the target's point. With false, the camera is at the target's point. The default is true.

strength.description: How far the camera moves toward the point it follows. 0 is not at all, and 1 is fully. It can be animated. The default is 1.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on. Without it, the camera follows exactly. A Position constraint's spring is written the same way as a keyframe's spring interpolation. `damping-ratio` and `response` are both required.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly the spring is damped. At 1, it is critically damped. With less damping, it swings farther.

response.description: The spring's natural period in seconds. A shorter response catches up sooner.

constraints.description: A model's or the camera's constraints in order. A model's constraints apply after its parent places it, and a node's as the node is posed. An override replaces the list. Each constraint's `strength` can be animated.

shape.description: Whether an area light is a rectangle or a disc. Either is `size.x` wide and `size.y` tall. In Redshift's Area Light, they are Rectangle and Disc.

light-type.description: What kind of light it is. A `directional` light shines from one direction, a `spot` in a cone from a point, a `point` every way from a point, and an `area` from a flat shape.

anyOf.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

intensity.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

anyOf.description: The full angle of a spot light's cone in degrees.

cone-angle.description: The full angle of a spot light's cone in degrees.

anyOf.description: How far in from a spot light's cone edge its light fades out. It is in degrees. 0 is a hard edge. The default is a quarter of the cone angle. Past half the cone angle, it fades over the whole cone.

falloff-angle.description: How far in from a spot light's cone edge its light fades out. It is in degrees. 0 is a hard edge. The default is a quarter of the cone angle. Past half the cone angle, it fades over the whole cone.

anyOf.description: The radius of a spot or point light in canvas units. A larger radius gives softer shadows. At 0, the shadows are crisp.

light-radius.description: The radius of a spot or point light in canvas units. A larger radius gives softer shadows. At 0, the shadows are crisp.

anyOf.description: The full angle in degrees that a directional light shines from. A wider angle gives softer shadows. The sun's disc spans about half a degree. At 0, the shadows are crisp.

light-angle.description: The full angle in degrees that a directional light shines from. A wider angle gives softer shadows. The sun's disc spans about half a degree. At 0, the shadows are crisp.

size.description: An area light's size is its width and height along its own axes in canvas units.

anyOf.description: The color of the shadows that a shadow catcher or a floor shows. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

shadow-color.description: The color of the shadows that a shadow catcher or a floor shows. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

anyOf.description: A shadow catcher's size along its own x in canvas units. A shadow catcher is a plane that shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it.

width.description: A shadow catcher's size along its own x in canvas units. A shadow catcher is a plane that shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it.

anyOf.description: A shadow catcher's size in canvas units along its own z when it lies flat, or along its own y when it is a wall.

height.description: A shadow catcher's size in canvas units along its own z when it lies flat, or along its own y when it is a wall.

orientation.description: Which way a shadow catcher faces when it isn't turned. With `y`, it lies flat and faces up. With `z`, it is a wall that faces the viewer. This matches Cinema 4D's Plane Orientation.

environment.description: The map that lights the 3D layer when the World has no color. The map's light is multiplied by the World's `intensity`. The World's `intensity` is 0 unless it is set. Each map is a file the format publishes.

anyOf.description: How far the World's map is turned about the y axis in degrees. It turns the way a 3D object's rotation y turns the object. It doesn't change a World with a color.

environment-rotation.description: How far the World's map is turned about the y axis in degrees. It turns the way a 3D object's rotation y turns the object. It doesn't change a World with a color.

overrides.description: Changes by id to what the slide inherits from its layout and master. They're kept even if they match what's inherited. An object set to `null` is removed. The camera and the World can't be removed.

anyOf.description: An object's id.

One object on a slide, a layout, or a master. Its keys depend on its type. Every chart can have any chart key, and every shape any shape key. A key that its chart type or shape kind doesn't use does nothing. A light can have only the keys its light type uses. An override needs none of the required keys because the object it changes already has them. In an override, a key set to null removes what the object inherits for that key. The key's default then shows.

frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide. It is in canvas units. Its x and y are from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y. A table's size comes from its contents, and an audio object's from its icon. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

z.description: How far in canvas units a text with a 3D `model` is in front of the slide. On a text without `model`, `z` does nothing. A model, light, camera, or shadow catcher is at its position's z.

anyOf.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored. A gradient is linear or radial.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

auto-size.description: Which sides of the text box grow to fit the text. The text never shrinks. A box set to grow can't animate its size or its text's layout, even on a path. InDesign's Auto-Size works the same way.

min-height.description: The minimum height in canvas units of a text box that grows in height. The box is as tall as its text or its `min-height`, whichever is taller. The text is placed inside the box by its vertical alignment.

column-count.description: The number of text columns. A column is at least 0 wide.

column-gutter.description: The space between text columns. It is in canvas units.

text-path.description: The path the text follows. It is SVG path data. The path's coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame. The text follows the path the same way as in Motion's Path layout method.

path-offset.description: How far the text moves along its path from where its `align` places it. It is in fractions of the path's length.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow behind the object. Without it, the object casts none. On a text, the shadow's lengths are in ems of the font size. The text's words, fill, and stroke cast it as one. A drop shadow's keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. The shadow starts as the shape of the letters, their outline, and the text box's fill and stroke. It grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches beyond what the text paints. It is in ems. Photoshop's Size works the same way.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

x.description: How far across. It is in ems.

y.description: How far down. It is in ems.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls in the text's own axes. The offset's x is across, and its y is down. It turns and scales with the text and its groups.

color.description: The shadow's color. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the object. Without it, the object casts none. On a text, the shadow's lengths are in ems of the font size. The text's words, fill, and stroke cast it as one.

model.description: The words as a 3D model. It is an `extrusion` that MarkdownPoint builds, or a GLB `file` that a program built. Where a `file` model's `built-from` doesn't match what it would be built from now, the text draws flat until the model is built again. A text with a model can't be in a group. An `extrusion` is built from the words' letters. Its `depth` and `bevel` are in ems of the text's size. A text on a path can't have an extrusion. If it has one, the extrusion is left out as the presentation is read and causes an `extrusion-with-text-path` warning. The text then draws flat. A `file` model's `built-from` is the fingerprint of what its GLB was built from. The fingerprint covers the text's words, the values of the fields they show, the presentation's `locale`, the family of each font role the words use and all the theme's files for that family, and the text's style and layout. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size. The model's origin is on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. For words on a path, the origin is the frame's top left. That is the path's 0 0, and the model's y points up from it. The model moves, turns, and scales with the text's frame. The text's `z` is how far the model is in front of the slide. The model's depth scales by the square root of the text's x scale times its y scale. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file` the same way they play any other model's. An extrusion has no Actions. Its letters are matte and lit only by the slide's lights and World. With no light and the World's intensity at 0, they draw black. The World's intensity is 0 by default.

frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide. It is in canvas units. Its x and y are from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y. A table's size comes from its contents, and an audio object's from its icon. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

column-widths.description: The width of each of a table's columns in order. The table is as wide as its columns. Without a list, or past its end, a column is 240 times the master's `default-scale` wide.

min-row-heights.description: The minimum height of each row. A row is taller when its words need more. A row of 0, or one past the list, has no minimum and is as tall as its words. The table is as tall as its rows.

header-row.description: Whether the table's first row is styled as a header.

header-column.description: Whether the table's first column is styled as a header.

alternating-rows.description: Whether every other row is shaded.

gridlines.description: Which of the table's lines show. With `none`, no lines show. With `horizontal`, the lines between rows show with the top and bottom edges. With `all`, every line shows with all four edges.

file.description: The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are.

mask.description: The shape the image is cut to. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the image's frame. The shape is filled by the nonzero rule.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated image is made with a transparent background.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated image. It is text without NUL characters.

image-style.description: The style a generated image is made in. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character, or "none". It isn't looked up in the style library. With `none`, the image has no style. `none` with white space at its ends is still `none`. The default is the presentation's `image-style`.

restyle.description: A style or an edit that the image model applies to the image as it was first made. It is a copy of a library style's `name`, `prompt`, and `transparent-background`, or the author's own. It isn't looked up in the style library. Until the restyle is applied, the image shows its `file` unchanged. Once the restyle is applied, `file` is the restyled image, and `restyled-from` names the image the restyle was applied to.

restyled-from.description: The image a restyle was applied to. It is an image in the presentation's media or generated folder. The image object's `file` is the restyled image. Once its `restyle` is removed, the image object shows this image again.

source.description: The code an image's picture is made from. An image with `source` is never generated from a prompt. Its `prompt`, `image-style`, `transparent-background`, `restyle`, and `restyled-from` are left out as the file is read. Each causes a `generation-with-source` warning. A save doesn't remove them. A program makes the picture only when an author asks it to. The image shows its `file`, whatever its code says. The `type` names the code's language.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the image's `file` was made from. It is written as `markdownpoint/<type>/<rule>:sha256:<hex>`. It ends with the SHA-256 of a record that has the `type` and `code` of the image's `source`. A diagram's fingerprint covers the master's body font too. The record's `font` is that font's name as the master's `fonts` spells it. When MarkdownPoint ships the font and the theme has no faces of its own for it, the name has MarkdownPoint's spelling, such as Inter for INTER. The record is written according to RFC 8785's JSON Canonicalization Scheme. A reader that doesn't know the fingerprint's rule treats the picture as out of date. Without `source`, the `built-from` is left out as the file is read. It then causes a `built-from-without-source` warning.

file.description: The path of the file the object shows or plays, such as a model's GLB. The file is in the presentation's folder. A master's or a layout's own image, video, audio, or model that isn't a placeholder can list one file for each color scheme.

audio-fade-in.description: How long a video's sound takes to rise linearly from silence each time the part set by `media-trim` starts to play. It is in seconds. The video's picture doesn't fade.

audio-fade-out.description: How long a video's sound takes to fall linearly to silence before the part set by `media-trim` ends each time. It is in seconds. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

poster-time.description: The time of the frame the video shows before it plays when it has no `poster`. It is in seconds from the start of the video's file. The default is the start of its `media-trim`.

anyOf.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored. A gradient is linear or radial.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

shape-type.description: Which shape a shape object draws. An edit that changes it drops each key the new kind doesn't use. A step that changes it drops none.

point-count.description: How many points a star has.

tail.description: Where a speech bubble's tail ends. It is in fractions of the bubble's frame.

geometry.description: The path's outline. It is SVG path data. Its coordinates from 0 to 1 span the object's frame.

fill-rule.description: Which areas of a self-crossing path the fill covers. A path used as a mask clips to the same areas.

anyOf.description: The color of the outline or the line. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. An image's or a video's outline follows its frame wherever the picture is inside it. A masked image's outline follows its mask. A path's stroke can be a gradient.

The color of the outline or the line. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. An image's or a video's outline follows its frame wherever the picture is inside it. A masked image's outline follows its mask. A path's stroke can be a gradient. A gradient is linear or radial.

stroke.description: The color of the outline or the line. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. An image's or a video's outline follows its frame wherever the picture is inside it. A masked image's outline follows its mask. A path's stroke can be a gradient.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

icon.description: The name of the Lucide 1.46.0 icon the object draws. It is the icon's own name, not an alias. A later version never drops a name.

anyOf.description: Where a line starts. The start is a point, or an object the line stays attached to. An attached end is straight out from the object's center toward its `side`. On a speech bubble or an object that isn't a shape, it meets the frame's edge. On any other shape, it meets the shape's outline.

start.description: Where a line starts. The start is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

anyOf.description: Where a line ends. The end is a point, or an object the line stays attached to. An attached end is straight out from the object's center toward its `side`. On a speech bubble or an object that isn't a shape, it meets the frame's edge. On any other shape, it meets the shape's outline.

end.description: Where a line ends. The end is a point, or an object the line stays attached to.

connection.description: How a line runs between its ends. An elbow line turns at right angles halfway between its ends.

bend.description: How far a curved line's middle bends from straight in multiples of the distance between its ends. A positive bend goes right, seen from the start toward the end.

cap-start.description: What the start of the line shows.

cap-end.description: What the end of the line shows.

anyOf.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored. A gradient is linear or radial.

color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color, or a record. Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

align.description: The text's horizontal alignment. Where neither the text nor its style sets one, lines align right when `text-direction` is `rtl`, and left otherwise. An explicit `left` stays left in right-to-left text. In a table, a column with no colons in the divider row uses the text style's alignment.

chart-type.description: Which chart the object draws. A column or a bar chart places each category's columns or bars side by side. A stacked column or bar chart stacks them. A line chart draws a line for each series, and a stacked area chart an area for each. A pie or a donut shows the first series. A counter shows the first value.

progress.description: How far the chart has grown in. A counter counts from 0 up to its value as `progress` rises.

delivery.description: How the chart's elements grow. With `by-element`, they grow one after another as `progress` rises. Without it, all grow at once.

spread.description: With `delivery`, how many intervals each element grows for. Without `delivery`, `spread` does nothing.

digits.description: How a counter's digits reach each value as it grows. With `change`, each digit changes in place. With `roll`, the digits roll into place like an odometer's.

value-labels.description: Where the chart labels its values. With `none`, it shows no value labels. With `auto`, each label shows past a bar's or a column's end, above or below a point, or inside a slice, a stacked segment, or a stacked area. A counter shows its figure either way.

legend.description: Where the chart shows a legend. With `none`, there is no legend. With `top`, it runs across the top of the chart. It names a pie's or a donut's categories, or any other chart's series.

series-colors.description: The colors of the chart's series in order. Every chart but a pie, a donut, or a counter uses them. For a `null` or missing entry, the chart uses the slide's colors by the entry's place: `accent` for the first, `text` for the second, and so on in turn. Where `accent` is the same color as `text` and `muted` isn't, `muted` takes the place of `text`. Each time the two repeat, they are drawn at a lower opacity.

category-colors.description: The colors of the chart's categories in order. A pie or a donut uses one for each slice.
