width.description: A shadow catcher's size along its own x in canvas units. A shadow catcher is a plane that shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it.

height.description: A shadow catcher's size in canvas units along its own z when it lies flat, or along its own y when it is a wall.

orientation.description: Which way a shadow catcher faces when it isn't turned. With `y`, it lies flat and faces up. With `z`, it is a wall that faces the viewer. This matches Cinema 4D's Plane Orientation.

position.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A floor is level and goes on without end. Like a shadow catcher, a floor shows only the shadows cast on it and hides the 3D objects behind it. Without a position, the floor is at the slide's bottom edge.

objects.description: The slide's objects, back to front. Each entry is an object's id or a record. The slide's own objects are written out, and an inherited one is listed by its id. An inherited one the list doesn't name is behind them all. An id listed twice is refused, and one the slide doesn't inherit is ignored with a warning.

propertyNames.description: An object's id, a dot, and a parameter, such as "card.opacity".

initial.description: Each animated parameter's value until a step animates it, or for the whole slide when none does. Each key is "object.parameter", such as "card.opacity". A `null` clears the whole parameter.

items.description: A step is the keyframes, cues, and effects that a click or the previous step sets off. Its times and those of its keyframes, cues, and effects are in seconds. They are rounded to six decimal places. A `start` of `with-previous` or `after-previous` works as PowerPoint's With Previous or After Previous. On the first step, either starts it as the slide's transition ends. A scroll into the slide plays the slide's first click with the move. The `start` of the slide's first step doesn't change that. A `play` or `clip` cue counts toward the step's length only at its own time. The step doesn't wait for what the cue starts to play through.

id.description: The step's id, such as "show-chart". It is unique on its slide.

name.description: The step's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

start.description: When the step starts. `on-click` starts it on a click of its own and is the default. `with-previous` starts it with the previous step. `after-previous` starts it after that step ends. The editor doesn't let a step that takes an object out of view start `with-previous` with that object's entrance. When a delete, a reorder, or an insertion would give a step that start, the editor sets its `start` to `after-previous`. A file can still have such a step. It plays as written and causes an `exit-joins-entrance` warning.

min-duration.description: The least time the step lasts in seconds. A keyframe, cue, effect, entering paragraph, or repeated copy past that time makes the step longer. Without a `min-duration`, or at 0, the step lasts as long as what is in it.

repeat-count.description: How many times the step plays. Without it, the step plays once. The step plays only as many times as fit in 4,294,967,296 seconds. A larger count causes a warning.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the step loops from `loop-start` to the end of its pass while it waits for a click. A step with a `repeat-count` starts its loop after its last pass. Without a loop, the step itself doesn't replay while it waits.

loop-start.description: How many seconds into the step the loop starts. Without a `loop-start`, the loop starts at 0. A `loop-start` at or past the end of one pass causes a `loop-start-past-end` warning, and the step doesn't loop.

propertyNames.description: An object's id, a dot, and a parameter, such as "card.opacity".

additionalProperties.description: A curve is one parameter's animation in a step. It has the parameter's keyframes and can loop after the last one. A position can also be keyed as one point. `frame.position` and `translation` have {x, y}, and `position` has {x, y, z}. Each of their keyframes has every part. A step keys a position either as a point or by its parts, not both. A step that keys both causes a `clashing-curves` warning, and the point plays. An initial value sets each part on its own.

A keyframe is a value a parameter reaches at a time. Its id is unique among the keyframes and cues of its step. Two keyframes of one parameter at one time cause a `clashing-keyframes` warning, and the one with the later id plays. A `begin` at or before the previous keyframe is ignored. On the first keyframe, a `begin` of 0 is ignored. A `discrete` key and interpolation `hold` have no move. A `begin` on either is ignored. An ignored `begin` must still come before `time`. A keyframe whose value is `null` clears the whole parameter at its time. The parameter's text style or default then shows. A `null` can't clear a part of a key, a point, `visible`, `rotation`, `scale`, a constraint's strength, `shape-type`, `icon`, or `geometry`. A `null` on a key that its object requires, such as a shadow catcher's `width` or a point light's `intensity`, causes an `ignored-animation-value` warning and is ignored. The same rules apply to `null` in a slide's `initial`. During a move toward `null`, the parameter stays at the value the move starts from. An `exponential-scale` move works as After Effects' Exponential Scale.

begin.description: When the keyframe's move begins. It is in seconds into the step. It must come before `time`. Without it, the move begins at the previous keyframe, or at 0 for the first keyframe.

time.description: When the parameter reaches the value. It is in seconds into the step.

value.description: The value the parameter reaches. It is written as the parameter is. It can be `null` to clear the whole parameter. It is the value itself and isn't measured from the object's own value.

anyOf.description: How the value reaches the keyframe. It is a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. With `hold`, the value jumps at the keyframe's time. The default is `linear`. An interpolation's settings say how far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past. They can also give an elastic's swing, a bounce's bounciness, a spring's damping ratio, or a cubic Bézier's two handles. The handles' keys are named the way CSS's cubic-bezier() names its four numbers. A named curve with no settings is written as its name alone. A cubic Bézier that is the same as a named curve is written as that named curve's name too.

amplitude.description: The size of an elastic's swing in multiples of the move. The default is 1.

period.description: How many seconds one swing of an elastic lasts. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `period` does nothing. The default is 0.3 of the length of the move.

bounciness.description: A bounce's rebound speed in fractions of its landing speed. At 0, it lands dead. At 0.5, the bounce is the same curve as Blender's Bounce. At 1, it rebounds to its height each time. The default is 0.5.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly a spring is damped. At 1, it doesn't swing past its keyframe. With less damping, it swings farther.

response.description: The spring's natural period in seconds. A shorter one springs faster. Without it, the spring settles by the end of the move. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `response` does nothing.

x1.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the move.

y1.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

x2.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the move.

y2.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

interpolation.description: How the value reaches the keyframe. It is a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. With `hold`, the value jumps at the keyframe's time. The default is `linear`.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts. The interrupted move goes from `begin` toward `interrupted.value`. Without the cut, it would arrive at `interrupted.time`. It is shaped by the keyframe's `interpolation`, `motion-path`, and `exponential-scale`. An elastic's period and a spring's settling are measured over that move. At the keyframe's `time` the move is cut, and the parameter has the keyframe's own `value`.

time.description: When the move would have reached `value`. It is in seconds into the step and at or after the keyframe's time. It doesn't make the step longer.

motion-path.description: A curved motion path for the keyframe's move. Only a point keyframe can have it. The path is in the move's own coordinates. 0 0 is where the move starts, and 1 0 is where it ends. Seen on the slide, the path's y points 90 degrees clockwise from its x. SVG's y does the same. So for a move to the right, a negative y bends the path up the slide.

geometry.description: The path of the move. It is SVG path data. The path runs from the move's start at 0 0 to its end at 1 0. It is one open contour of 2 to 8,192 points and has at most 2,097,152 characters.

orient.description: Whether the object turns to face along the path. The default is false.

exponential-scale.description: Whether a scale move changes by a steady ratio. A zoom then looks even. A move that starts at 0, ends at 0, or crosses 0 plays as it would without `exponential-scale`. `exponential-scale` applies only to `scale`, `scale.x`, `scale.y`, `scale.z`, and `crop.scale`.

keyframes.description: The keyframes by id, one or more. They are ordered by their time, then by their id.

loop.description: How the curve loops after its last keyframe until the step ends. With `repeat`, the curve replays from `loop-keyframe` to the last keyframe. With `ping-pong`, it plays that part back and forth. Without a loop, it plays once.

loop-keyframe.description: The id of the keyframe the loop starts at, such as "card-settles". If the keyframe has a `begin`, the loop begins with its move. If the id names no keyframe of the curve, the first keyframe is used.

curves.description: The step's animation. Each curve is under an "object.parameter" key such as card.opacity.

additionalProperties.description: An event at a set time in a step. Its id is unique among the keyframes and cues of its step. A `paragraph` cue shows a paragraph of a text or a shape. A `play` cue starts an audio object, a video, or a web video. A `clip` cue plays an Action of the GLB `file` of a model or a 3D text. A cue on an object of any other type is ignored. It causes an `ignored-animation` warning. A clip works as Cinema 4D's Motion Clip. A text built from an `extrusion` has no Actions. A clip on it plays nothing and causes a warning.

paragraph.description: The id of the paragraph that appears. It is the id in the `<!-- id: … -->` at the end of the paragraph's last line or alone on the line after it. A list item's id ends its first paragraph. A reader warns when no paragraph of the text has the id.

action.description: The name of the Action that a clip plays. An unnamed Action is named Animation and its number in the file, as in `Animation 1` for the first. A clip naming an Action its object doesn't have plays nothing. It causes an `unknown-action` warning.

loop.description: With `repeat`, the Action plays again from the start of its `clip-trim` each time it ends. Without a loop or a `stride`, even an Action made to repeat plays once. A model's clip with a `stride` is timed by the model's travel whether or not it has a loop.

clip-trim.description: The part of the Action that plays. It is a start and an end in seconds.

stride.description: How far the model travels per cycle of its Action. It is in the GLB's meters. With a `stride`, the Action's timing follows the model's travel. A 3D text's clip with a `stride` is ignored. It causes an `ignored-animation` warning.

blend-in.description: How many seconds the clip takes to blend in fully over the model's current motion. Without it, or at 0, the clip is fully blended in from its start.

clip-scale.description: How long a clip takes to play through its part of the Action in multiples of that part's length. The part is the clip's `clip-trim`, or the whole Action without one. 2 is half speed, and 0.5 is double. Maya's Clip Scale works the same way. A clip with a `stride` doesn't use it. The default is 1.

cues.description: The step's cues by id. They are ordered by their time, then by their id. A cue shows a paragraph, plays a clip, or starts an audio object, a video, or a web video.

additionalProperties.description: An object's effect in a step is an entrance, an exit, or an emphasis by name. It plays as keyframes from where the object is as the effect starts. In a step that starts with or after another, the effect starts from where the earlier steps of the click have the object at the effect's `delay`. When no initial value or earlier step keys a parameter that an entrance runs, and none shows, hides, or reveals the entrance's object, the parameter has the entrance's starting value from the slide's start until the object enters. After an exit ends, the object stays as the exit left it. An emphasis returns the object to where it started. A `pieces` entrance or exit brings in or takes out a text's paragraphs, words, or characters in the look of the text's `enter` or `exit`. An effect that keys what its object can't animate causes an `ignored-animation` warning and plays nothing.

effect.description: Which effect it is. An entrance can `appear`, `fade`, `rise`, `scale`, `blur`, `draw` a stroke, `wipe`, `grow` a chart, or bring in a text's `pieces`. An exit can `disappear`, `fade`, `sink`, `scale`, `blur`, or take out a text's `pieces`. An emphasis can `pulse`, `bounce`, `blink`, or `spin`.

Which effect it is. An entrance can `appear`, `fade`, `rise`, `scale`, `blur`, `draw` a stroke, `wipe`, `grow` a chart, or bring in a text's `pieces`. An exit can `disappear`, `fade`, `sink`, `scale`, `blur`, or take out a text's `pieces`. An emphasis can `pulse`, `bounce`, `blink`, or `spin`.

Which effect it is. An entrance can `appear`, `fade`, `rise`, `scale`, `blur`, `draw` a stroke, `wipe`, `grow` a chart, or bring in a text's `pieces`. An exit can `disappear`, `fade`, `sink`, `scale`, `blur`, or take out a text's `pieces`. An emphasis can `pulse`, `bounce`, `blink`, or `spin`.

effects.description: The step's effects by object id. Each id has one effect. An effect is an entrance, an exit, or an emphasis by name. An object's effect and its own keyframes don't go together in one step. The effect plays, and the keyframes cause a `clashing-curves` warning and don't play.

slides.description: The slides by id. The .md file has their order and text.

additionalProperties.description: A comment pinned to a slide. It can have replies. Its id is unique among the presentation's comments.

slide.description: The id of the slide the comment is pinned to, such as "title-card". It can name a slide that is no longer there.

author.description: Who wrote the comment or reply. In an author's `id`, `local:` is for a computer's user, `dropbox:` for a Dropbox user, and `microsoft:` for a Microsoft account user. A Dropbox account id is spelled as Dropbox's API spells it. It is `dbid:` followed by one or more of A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9, `_`, and `-`. A Microsoft account id is the account's Microsoft Graph id in lowercase. It is a UUID for a work or school account and 16 hexadecimal digits for a personal account.

created.description: The time the comment or reply was written. It is a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as "2026-10-17T19:30:00.000Z".

text.description: What the comment or reply says. The text isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs. Its line breaks are line feeds. A carriage return, alone or before a line feed, is read as a line feed.

x.description: How far across. It is in canvas units.

y.description: How far down. It is in canvas units.

position.description: Where on the slide the comment is pinned. The position's x and y are in canvas units. When the slide size changes, the comment moves with the slide's objects.

resolved.description: Whether the comment is resolved. The default is false.

additionalProperties.description: One reply to a comment. Its id is unique among the comment's replies.

author.description: Who wrote the comment or reply. In an author's `id`, `local:` is for a computer's user, `dropbox:` for a Dropbox user, and `microsoft:` for a Microsoft account user. A Dropbox account id is spelled as Dropbox's API spells it. It is `dbid:` followed by one or more of A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9, `_`, and `-`. A Microsoft account id is the account's Microsoft Graph id in lowercase. It is a UUID for a work or school account and 16 hexadecimal digits for a personal account.

created.description: The time the comment or reply was written. It is a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as "2026-10-17T19:30:00.000Z".

text.description: What the comment or reply says. The text isn't blank and has no control characters except line breaks and tabs. Its line breaks are line feeds. A carriage return, alone or before a line feed, is read as a line feed.

replies.description: The replies by id. They are ordered by their `created` time, then by their id. Each has an author, a created time, and text.

comments.description: Comments by id. They are ordered by their `created` time, then by their id. Each one is pinned to a slide.

anchor-point.x.description: How far across the box in fractions of its width.

anchor-point.y.description: How far down the box in fractions of its height.

area-size.x.description: The width along the light's own x in canvas units. The default is 100 times the master's `default-scale`.

area-size.y.description: The height along the light's own y in canvas units. The default is 100 times the master's `default-scale`.

back.description: How far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past. Robert Penner's back curves and Blender's Back use it the same way. The default is 1.70158.

anyOf.description: A color role or a hex color.

id.description: The author's id, if known. It is "local:" followed by a lowercase UUID, "dropbox:" followed by a Dropbox account id that starts with "dbid:", or "microsoft:" followed by a Microsoft account id that is a lowercase UUID or 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

name.description: The name the comment shows for the author. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target. Cinema 4D's Aim constraint works the same way. Every key except `id`, `type`, and `target` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as "look". It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.<id>.strength`.

node.description: The name of the node that turns, such as Head. Without it, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light to turn toward. With `camera`, the camera is the target.

target-node.description: The name of the node in the target's model to turn toward, such as Hand. The model or node turns toward that node as the target's Action moves it. Without `target-node`, the model or node turns toward the target's origin.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target. It is one of the model's or node's own axes in the GLB. In a model's GLB, y is up, and the model faces along +z. The default is `z`.

strength.description: How far the model or node turns toward the target. 0 is not at all, and 1 is fully. The strength applies to the result of the constraints before this one. It can be animated. The default is 1.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as the model scales along its own axes. The volume is measured at the model's `scale` as the object sets it, before any `initial` value or step. An axis the constraint scales stops at a 3D scale's limit of 1 × 10¹⁸ either way, and an axis at 0 stays at 0. Every key except `id` and `type` can be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as "look". It is unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as `constraints.<id>.strength`.

mode.description: When the volume is kept. With `strict`, it always is. With `uniform`, it is kept while the model scales evenly. With `single-axis`, it is kept while only the free axis scales. The three modes are those of Blender's Maintain Volume constraint. The default is `strict`.

free-axis.description: The axis the constraint leaves as it is. The constraint scales the other two to keep the volume. The default is `y`.

volume.description: The volume to keep. It is a multiple of the model's volume at its `scale`. At 0.4, the model is squeezed to 40% of its volume. The default is 1.

strength.description: How strongly the constraint keeps the volume. 0 is not at all, and 1 is fully. It can be animated. The default is 1.

scale.description: How far the image or video is zoomed. At 1, an image fits its frame as its `scale-mode` sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1, it is zoomed in. At 2, it is twice as wide and twice as tall as at 1. Below 1, it is zoomed out. The default is 1.

focal-point.description: The point that stays in view. The focal point's x and y are fractions of the picture's width and height. The default is x 0.5 and y 0.5.

x.description: How far across the picture in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the picture in fractions of its height.

cue.object.description: The id of the object the cue acts on.

cue.time.description: When the cue happens. It is in seconds into the step.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

delivery.description: With `by-paragraph`, each paragraph enters on the step whose paragraph cue names it. `by-paragraph` needs based-on `paragraph` and no seed. Order, spread, pause, and progress must be at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter in seconds. With interpolation hold, `duration` is still required but isn't used. A step that has only paragraph cues lasts as long as its paragraphs take to enter.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter. Without a `from`, each piece fades in. Motion's Sequence Text with Sequencing From works the same way.

opacity.description: How opaque the piece is. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far a piece starts from where it rests. A piece's offset is in ems of the piece's own font size. The offset's x is across, and its y is down. On a path, x is along the path, and y is across it, toward the letters' feet. For a text drawn as its 3D model, x is still across and y is still down. The default is x 0 and y 0.

scale.description: The piece's scale. At 1, the piece is its own size. The default is 1.

rotation.description: How far the piece is turned in degrees clockwise. The default is 0.

blur.description: How blurred the piece is. It is the blur's radius in ems of the piece's own font size. The default is 0.

anyOf.description: How each piece moves into place. With `hold`, it moves instantly. With any other interpolation, it moves gradually. The default is `linear`. An interpolation's settings say how far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past. They can also give an elastic's swing, a bounce's bounciness, a spring's damping ratio, or a cubic Bézier's two handles. The handles' keys are named the way CSS's cubic-bezier() names its four numbers. A named curve with no settings is written as its name alone. A cubic Bézier that is the same as a named curve is written as that named curve's name too.

amplitude.description: The size of an elastic's swing in multiples of the move. The default is 1.

period.description: How many seconds one swing of an elastic lasts. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `period` does nothing. The default is 0.3 of the length of the move.

bounciness.description: A bounce's rebound speed in fractions of its landing speed. At 0, it lands dead. At 0.5, the bounce is the same curve as Blender's Bounce. At 1, it rebounds to its height each time. The default is 0.5.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly a spring is damped. At 1, it doesn't swing past its keyframe. With less damping, it swings farther.

response.description: The spring's natural period in seconds. A shorter one springs faster. Without it, the spring settles by the end of the move. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `response` does nothing.

x1.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the move.

y1.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

x2.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the move.

y2.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place. With `hold`, it moves instantly. With any other interpolation, it moves gradually. The default is `linear`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's entrance that the fade lasts. The fade starts with the move and follows the piece's interpolation. The default is 1.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in. With a seed, it must be `random`. The default is `forward`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order. The same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for unless the interpolation is `hold`. With `hold`, each piece arrives once its start has passed, and an entrance without a `delivery` ends this many intervals after the last one starts. With any other interpolation and a forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once. The default is 1.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. With a `pause` above 0, the turns start `pause` + `spread` − 1 intervals farther apart than with no pause. The default is 0.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. `progress` is animated by steps. It isn't animated when the entrance has a `delivery`. The default is 1.

based-on.description: What counts as one piece. With `character-and-space`, each space is a piece too. After Effects' Characters is `character-and-space`, and its Characters Excluding Spaces is `character`.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting. Without a `to`, each piece fades out. Motion's Sequence Text with Sequencing To works the same way.

opacity.description: How opaque the piece is. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far a piece ends from where it rests. A piece's offset is in ems of the piece's own font size. The offset's x is across, and its y is down. On a path, x is along the path, and y is across it, toward the letters' feet. For a text drawn as its 3D model, x is still across and y is still down. The default is x 0 and y 0.

scale.description: The piece's scale. At 1, the piece is its own size. The default is 1.

rotation.description: How far the piece is turned in degrees clockwise. The default is 0.

blur.description: How blurred the piece is. It is the blur's radius in ems of the piece's own font size. The default is 0.

anyOf.description: How each piece moves out of place. With `hold`, it moves instantly. With any other interpolation, it moves gradually. The default is `linear`. An interpolation's settings say how far `anticipate`, `overshoot`, or `anticipate-overshoot` pulls back or swings past. They can also give an elastic's swing, a bounce's bounciness, a spring's damping ratio, or a cubic Bézier's two handles. The handles' keys are named the way CSS's cubic-bezier() names its four numbers. A named curve with no settings is written as its name alone. A cubic Bézier that is the same as a named curve is written as that named curve's name too.

amplitude.description: The size of an elastic's swing in multiples of the move. The default is 1.

period.description: How many seconds one swing of an elastic lasts. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `period` does nothing. The default is 0.3 of the length of the move.

bounciness.description: A bounce's rebound speed in fractions of its landing speed. At 0, it lands dead. At 0.5, the bounce is the same curve as Blender's Bounce. At 1, it rebounds to its height each time. The default is 0.5.

damping-ratio.description: How strongly a spring is damped. At 1, it doesn't swing past its keyframe. With less damping, it swings farther.

response.description: The spring's natural period in seconds. A shorter one springs faster. Without it, the spring settles by the end of the move. In a text's `enter` and `exit`, `response` does nothing.

x1.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the move.

y1.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's first handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

x2.description: The time of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the move.

y2.description: The value of a cubic Bézier's second handle in fractions of the change. It can be below 0 or above 1. The move can then go past an end. It stops at the end of the parameter's range.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place. With `hold`, it moves instantly. With any other interpolation, it moves gradually. The default is `linear`.

fade.description: The fraction of each piece's exit that the fade lasts. The fade ends with the move and follows the piece's interpolation. The default is 1.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in. With a seed, it must be `random`. The default is `forward`.

seed.description: The seed for a random order. The same seed gives the same order. The default is 0.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for unless the interpolation is `hold`. With `hold`, each piece leaves once its start has passed, and the exit ends this many intervals after the last one starts. With any other interpolation and a forward, backward, or random order, this many pieces move at once. The default is 1.

pause.description: How many intervals the text waits between turns. With a `pause` above 0, the turns start `pause` + `spread` − 1 intervals farther apart than with no pause. The default is 0.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. `progress` is animated by steps. The default is 0.

flat-scale.x.description: How far the object is stretched along its own x.

flat-scale.y.description: How far the object is stretched along its own y.

floor-position.y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge in canvas units.

frame.height.description: The height. It is in canvas units.

frame.width.description: The width. It is in canvas units.

frame.x.description: How far across the slide the left edge is. It is in canvas units. When a text box's width grows, x is the point its text is aligned to.

frame.y.description: How far down the slide the top edge is. It is in canvas units. When a text box's height grows, its default `anchor-point` is on its top edge.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line is. Its middle and length are in the box the object is drawn at, not in the box the gradient spans. A background's box is the slide, and a gradient on a shape's words uses the shape's frame. The line turns about its middle by `angle`. By default, it crosses the box the gradient spans through that box's center. CSS's gradient line works the same way.

x.description: The x of the line's middle in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: The y of the line's middle in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

length.description: How long the line is. It is in box diagonals.

center.description: The x and y of a radial gradient's center. The center is in the box the object is drawn at. It can be outside that box. A linear gradient's `line` is in the same box. The center doesn't move while a path's outline morphs. A background's box is the slide, and a gradient on a shape's words uses the shape's frame. The gradient reaches whichever corner of the box it spans is farthest from its center. CSS's `farthest-corner` works the same way.

x.description: The center's x in fractions of the box's width. 0 is the left edge, and 1 is the right edge.

y.description: The center's y in fractions of the box's height. 0 is the top edge, and 1 is the bottom edge.

shape.description: With `circle`, a radial gradient is round in any box. Without `shape`, it is an ellipse.

gradient.stops.description: The gradient's two or more colors and their positions.

object.description: The attached object's id. It names an object on the same slide.

side.description: Which side of the object's frame the end attaches to. The sides turn with the object's `rotation`, and a flip doesn't change them. With `auto`, the end attaches to the side that faces the line's other end.

object.align.description: The text's horizontal alignment. Where neither the text nor its style sets one, lines align right when `text-direction` is `rtl`, and left otherwise. An explicit `left` stays left in right-to-left text. In a table, a column with no colons in the divider row uses the text style's alignment.

object.alt.description: A description of the object that screen readers read aloud. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks. On a shape or a table, the description is read before the words. On a chart, it is read in place of the labels. Without `alt`, an image whose picture matches its code is described by that code on one line. When an edit in MarkdownPoint changes an icon's own `icon` key, the edit removes the icon's `alt` too. An `alt` given in the same edit stays. A step's keyframe for `icon` leaves `alt` as it is. When an edit gives an image or a video another `file`, the edit removes the object's `alt` too. When the object inherits an `alt`, the edit sets `alt` to null in its override. `alt` stays as it is when an edit applies or removes a restyle, gives the image its `restyled-from` file, renames or moves the object's file, gives the image a copy of its file to open in an image editor, or gives a theme's image or video a file for one color scheme. When an edit removes the `file` of an object that isn't inherited, the edit removes its `alt` too. When an edit resets or removes a `file` that an override gives, the edit removes the override's `alt` too. The object then has the `alt` it inherits. An edit that removes an inherited `file`, or resets a `null` `file` alone, leaves `alt` as it is because that `alt` describes what the inherited `file` shows. None of these edits changes the `alt` of an image with `source` because its picture is made from its code. An `alt` given after the `file` in the same edit stays. A change written directly into the presentation's files leaves `alt` as it is too.

object.anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about. 0.5, 0.5 is the center. A group and a text with a 3D `model` also tilt about it. It is in fractions of the box the object is drawn at. A growing text box is drawn at the size of its words, and a group at its box. A table is drawn at its columns' widths and its rows' heights. Any other object is drawn at its frame. Without an `anchor-point`, an object turns and scales about its center. A text box that grows turns and scales about the point its text grows from. Leaving out `anchor-point` is the only way to get the default.

object.blend-mode.description: How the object's colors combine with what is under it. Each mode except a group's `pass-through` is the CSS `mix-blend-mode` of that name. The modes are defined in Compositing and Blending Level 1.

object.blur.description: The radius of the object's Gaussian blur in canvas units.

object.bullet-styles.description: The bullet at each list level in order from the first. There is at least one. The last one is used at every deeper level.

object.case.description: The letter case the text is shown in. The text itself stays as typed. With `capitalize`, each word starts with a capital.

object.cast-shadow.description: Whether a model or a text with a 3D `model` casts shadows. On a light, whether it casts the shadows of the models and texts that cast them. On a text without `model`, `cast-shadow` does nothing.

object.color.description: The color of the text, icon, light, or World, or the single color of an SVG image. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". Text, shapes, and charts can use a gradient. A light's or the World's color has no alpha. On a light or the World, a role's alpha is ignored.

object.constrain-proportions.description: Whether the object's scale, or a group's size, keeps its proportions when one side changes.

object.corner-radius.description: The radius of a rectangle's, an image's, or a video's corners in canvas units. An image's or a video's corners are its frame's. A masked image's radius isn't drawn until its mask is removed.

object.crop.description: How far the image or video is zoomed inside its frame, and which point stays in view.

object.decorative.description: Whether screen readers skip the object as decoration. A decorative shape's words and a decorative chart's labels are skipped too. Without `alt`, an image, video, web video, model, icon, or chart that isn't decorative causes a warning once it has something to show. A counter causes no warning because screen readers read its figure. An image whose picture matches its code causes none either.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow behind the object. Without it, the object casts none. On a text, the shadow's lengths are in ems of the font size. The text's words, fill, and stroke cast it as one. A drop shadow's keys work like those of Photoshop's Drop Shadow. The shadow starts as the shape of what casts it. It grows solid by size × spread. Then it is blurred by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. The size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far the shadow reaches in canvas units.

spread.description: The fraction of the size that is solid. The rest of the size is blurred. At 1, the shadow is solid all the way out. Photoshop's Spread works the same way. The default is 0.

offset.description: How far the shadow falls in the object's own axes. The offset's x is across, and its y is down. It turns and scales with the object and its groups. A flip doesn't mirror it. Because a line has no `rotation`, its offset is in the slide's axes and scales with the line's groups. A background's offset is in the slide's axes.

color.description: The shadow's color. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadow's opacity is set by `opacity` alone.

object.drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the object. Without it, the object casts none. On a text, the shadow's lengths are in ems of the font size. The text's words, fill, and stroke cast it as one.

object.enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece. A piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. `based-on` sets which. `delivery: by-paragraph` works the same way as PowerPoint's By Paragraph.

object.exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece. A piece is a paragraph, a word, or a character. An exit's pieces are counted and timed the same way as an entrance's.

anyOf.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells, or in a text's frame behind its words. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. A text's words have their own color over the fill. With `none`, there is no fill. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells, or in a text's frame behind its words. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. A text's words have their own color over the fill. With `none`, there is no fill. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record. A gradient is linear or radial.

object.fill.description: The paint inside the shape, path, or table cells, or in a text's frame behind its words. It is none, a color role or a hex color, or a record. A text's words have their own color over the fill. With `none`, there is no fill. A gradient fill is written as a `gradient` record.

object.flip.description: How the object's picture, glyph, or outline is mirrored along its own axes. An image's `mask`, a shape's gradients, and a shape's text aren't mirrored.

object.font-family.description: The font role the text uses. The theme sets a font family for each role. On a chart, the role sets every label's font. Keynote's Chart Font works the same way.

object.font-size.description: The font size. It is in canvas units.

object.font-style.description: Whether the text's letters stand upright with `normal` or lean with `italic`. They lean only in a family with an italic face.

object.font-weight.description: How bold the text's letters are. 100 is thin, 200 extra light, 300 light, 400 regular, 500 medium, 600 semibold, 700 bold, 800 extra bold, and 900 black. Each character is drawn in the face that CSS Fonts Level 4's font matching chooses for the text's weight and style among the faces of the family that draws it. MarkdownPoint never makes a face bolder to make up for a weight the family lacks.

object.frame.description: The object's position and size on the slide. It is in canvas units. Its x and y are from the top left of its slide. A table's and an audio object's frame has only x and y. A table's size comes from its contents, and an audio object's from its icon. A text box's frame leaves out each side that grows to fit its text. An audio object's frame is the top left of its icon. The icon shows only while editing. It has the same size at any zoom.

object.grayscale.description: How far the colors fade to gray.

object.id.description: The object's id. It is unique on its slide. Only the camera has the id `camera`, and only the World has the id `world`.

object.inset.description: The space in canvas units between the words and the edges of a text's frame, a table cell, or a shape's text area. A shape's text area is the box in its frame where its words go. On a rectangle or a speech bubble, it is the whole frame. A rectangle's rounded corners don't change it. On an ellipse, it is the largest rectangle that fits inside the ellipse. On a diamond, it is centered and is half as wide and half as tall as the diamond. On a triangle, it is half as wide and half as tall as the triangle. It is centered across the triangle, and its bottom edge is on the triangle's base. On a hexagon, it is a sixth of the frame in from each side. On a chevron, it runs from the point of the notch to the shoulders. On an arrow, it is the shaft and reaches into the head until the shaft's edges meet the head's sides. On a double arrow, it is the shaft and reaches into both heads the same way. On a star, it starts as the box around the inner corners. That box shrinks toward its center until no inner corner is inside it and its corners are inside the star. When the shape is flipped, its text area is mirrored with it. On a shape, `inset` places the text box inside the text area, and `padding-top` and `padding-bottom` add space inside that box. On a text, `inset` pads the words on every side, and `padding-top` and `padding-bottom` add to it above the first line and below the last. A text on a path doesn't use `inset`.

object.intensity.description: How bright a light or the World is. For a point, spot, or area light, it is in watts. For a directional light or the World, the color is multiplied by it.

object.kerning.description: Whether the font's kerning sets the space between letters. With `none`, it works as InDesign's Kerning 0.

object.light-radius.description: The radius of a spot or point light in canvas units. A larger radius gives softer shadows. At 0, the shadows are crisp.

object.line-height.description: The distance between lines in multiples of the font size.

object.link.description: Where a click on the object goes while presenting. A link works when it is an http:// or https:// URL with a host, a mailto: or tel: address, or slide: followed by a slide's id. A link that works has no spaces or control characters, and an http or https one has no backslash. Any other link is kept as written and does nothing. A link to a skipped slide does nothing in the show or in a PDF until the slide is shown again.

object.list-indent.description: How far each list level indents. It is in canvas units.

object.locked.description: Whether the object is locked against selection and editing on the canvas.

object.loop.description: With `repeat`, the video or audio plays again from the start of its `media-trim` each time it ends. Without a loop, it plays once. A video then stays on the frame where it stops.

object.media-trim.description: The part of the video or audio file that plays. It is a start and an end in seconds.

object.name.description: The object's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

object.number-spacing.description: How wide the digits are. With `default`, each digit has its font's width. With `tabular`, all digits have the same width. Numbers then line up in columns. Word's number spacing works the same way.

object.padding-bottom.description: The space between the text box's last line and its bottom. It is in canvas units.

object.padding-top.description: The space between the text box's top and its first line. It is in canvas units.

object.paragraph-spacing.description: The space between paragraphs. It is in canvas units.

object.parent.description: The id of the group, model, or light the object is parented to. The frames and ends of a group's members are in the slide's coordinates. A model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with its parent model or light.

object.parent-inverse.description: The matrix that leaves the object where it was when it was parented. It has 16 numbers, column by column. Its fourth row is 0, 0, 0, and 1. Those are its 4th, 8th, 12th, and 16th numbers.

object.parent-node.description: The node of the parent model that a model, a light, a shadow catcher, or the camera moves with. It is the name of one of the model's nodes. Without it, the object moves with the whole model.

object.placeholder-layout.description: The layout the object came from. When the slide's layout or theme changes and a filled placeholder goes away, MarkdownPoint leaves the placeholder's words, image, or video in place as the slide's own object. An object that still has the placeholder's id is marked with the layout it left. When the layout or theme changes again and the slide has a placeholder with a marked object's id, MarkdownPoint puts the object back into that placeholder. A text goes only into a text placeholder, and an image or a video only into an image or a video placeholder.

object.point-of-interest.description: The point the camera or a directional, spot, or area light faces. It is used in place of the rotation. It is in the position's space. The camera's or light's top stays toward the top of that space. A point in the 3D space is in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

object.position.description: Where the object is in the 3D space. Y is up. It places a model's origin, or the center of a light, the camera, or a shadow catcher. A floor's position is its height. It is written as y. A point in the 3D space is in canvas units. The x axis runs right from the slide's left edge, the y axis runs up from its bottom edge, and the z axis runs toward the viewer. The slide is at z 0. The axes are right-handed. glTF and three.js use the same axes. After Effects' y and z axes run the other way. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

object.poster.description: The path to the image the video shows before it plays. The file is a supported image in the presentation's media or generated folder, such as "media/photo.png". Without a `poster`, a video shows the frame at `poster-time`, and a web video its provider's image. An override that sets a video's `poster` or `poster-time` replaces both.

object.repeater.description: Copies of the object. Each is moved, turned, scaled, and delayed from the one before. The original stays as written.

object.rotation.description: How far a flat object is turned about its `anchor-point` in degrees clockwise. A group's rotation is the angle its box is measured at. A 3D object's rotation is in the form its `rotation-mode` sets.

object.rotation-mode.description: The form of a 3D object's rotation. Without it, the rotation is in degrees in Cinema 4D's HPB order. With `quaternion`, it is written as w, x, y, and z in its space's axes.

object.scale.description: How far the object is stretched along its own axes. It has x and y on a flat object, and x, y, and z on a model or a light. A flat object scales about its `anchor-point`. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

object.scale-mode.description: How an image or video fills its frame. With `fill`, it covers the frame and the rest is cropped. With `fit`, all of it shows inside the frame.

object.shadow-color.description: The color of the shadows that a shadow catcher or a floor shows. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's alpha is ignored. The shadows' opacity is set by `opacity`.

object.start-on.description: With `cue`, the video, audio, or web video starts at a `play` cue. With `slide`, it starts once the transition into its slide has ended, or with the step that first shows it. No `play` cue starts it then.

object.stroke.description: The color of the outline or the line. It is a color role or a hex color. An image's or a video's outline follows its frame wherever the picture is inside it. A masked image's outline follows its mask. A path's stroke can be a gradient.

object.stroke-style.description: Whether the outline or the line is solid, dashed, or dotted.

object.stroke-weight.description: How thick the outline or the line is in canvas units. An icon's weight is its line weight in icon units.

object.text-direction.description: Which way every paragraph of the text runs. With `ltr`, it runs left to right. With `rtl`, it runs right to left. Arabic and Hebrew use `rtl`. Lists, quotes, and columns start on the same side as the text.

object.text-stroke.description: The color of a stroke around each letter. It is a color role or a hex color. Keynote's text Outline works the same way.

object.text-stroke-weight.description: The thickness of the stroke around each letter in ems.

object.text-style.description: The name of the object's text style in the master's `text-styles`. No name is built in. A name the master lacks causes an `unknown-text-style` warning. The text then has no text style.

object.tilt.description: How far a group or a text with a 3D `model` tilts in depth. The object turns about axes parallel to the slide through its anchor point. Inside a tilted group, they are parallel to that group's picture. The tilt is in degrees. A group's picture is seen in perspective through a 50 mm lens from in front of its anchor point. The slide's camera doesn't change that perspective. A text's model turns in the slide's 3D space about the text's anchor point at the text's `z`. The model is seen through the slide's camera. The text's words and their links are on the turned plane. On a text without `model`, `tilt` does nothing.

object.tracking.description: Extra space between letters. It is in ems.

object.trim.description: The drawn part of the stroke. A trim runs from `start` to `end` along a path's or a line's stroke.

object.use-as-mask.description: Whether the shape or path clips the members after it in its group to its outline.

object.vertical-align.description: The text's vertical alignment in its box. Text in more than one column always sits at the top.

object.visible.description: Whether the object shows on the slide. A hidden light is off, and a hidden video, web video, or audio object doesn't play. A step can't animate it on an audio object or a light.

object.volume.description: How loud the video or audio plays. 1 is the file's own level.

object.wipe.description: A straight edge that reveals the object as its progress rises from 0 to 1.

picture-source.code.description: The code the picture is made from. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character. With `latex`, the code is display math in LaTeX with the amsmath and amssymb packages. The `\[` and `\]` around it are left out. With `mermaid`, the code is a diagram in the syntax of Mermaid 12.1.0.

piece-offset.x.description: How far across in ems of the piece's own font size. For a text that draws flat on a path, it is how far along the path.

piece-offset.y.description: How far down in ems of the piece's own font size. For a text that draws flat on a path, it is how far across the path, toward the letters' feet.

point.x.description: How far across. It is in canvas units.

point.y.description: How far down. It is in canvas units.

copies.description: How many copies there are. The original counts as one.

x.description: How far across. It is in canvas units.

y.description: How far down. It is in canvas units.

position.description: The move from each copy to the next. Its x is across, and its y is down. It is measured in the turned and scaled axes of the copy before. The default is x 0 and y 0.

rotation.description: How far each copy is turned clockwise from the one before. It is in degrees. The default is 0.

scale.description: How much each copy is scaled from the one before. At 1, each copy is the same size as the one before. The default is 1.

anchor-point.description: The point the copies turn and scale about with `rotation` and `scale`. The anchor point's x and y are fractions of the width and height of the box the object is drawn at. For a group, that box is the group's box. The default is x 0.5 and y 0.5.

x.description: How far across the box in fractions of its width.

y.description: How far down the box in fractions of its height.

stagger.description: How many seconds each copy waits after the one before it to start the object's animation. A copy starts the animation at most (`copies` − 1) × `stagger` + `stagger-randomness` seconds after the original. Keyframes of the object's own `repeater` aren't delayed. They lay out every copy at once. The default is 0.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity. It is a fraction of the object's opacity. The copies between fade toward it evenly. After Effects' End Opacity works the same way with a Start Opacity of 100%. The default is 1.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction. It is in canvas units. The default is 0.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random about its own center. It is in degrees. Motion's Replicator Angle Randomness works the same way. The default is 0.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random about its own center. It is a fraction of the copy's size. The default is 0.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random. It is in seconds. The default is 0.

seed.description: The random seed. The same seed gives the same copies. Motion's Random Seed works the same way. The default is 0.

name.description: The style's name. It is one line that isn't blank and has no control characters or line breaks.

prompt.description: The edit prompt that says how the style changes an image. It is text that isn't blank and has no NUL character.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds. The default is false.

space-position.x.description: How far across. It is in canvas units.

space-position.y.description: How far up. It is in canvas units.

space-position.z.description: How far toward the viewer. It is in canvas units.

w.description: A quaternion's w. It is used in quaternion mode only.

space-rotation.x.description: The turn about x in degrees, or a quaternion's x.

space-rotation.y.description: The turn about y in degrees, or a quaternion's y.

space-rotation.z.description: The turn about z in degrees, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.x.description: How far the object is stretched along its own x.

space-scale.y.description: How far the object is stretched along its own y.

space-scale.z.description: How far the object is stretched along its own z.

step-effect.delay.description: How many seconds into the step the effect starts. Without it, the effect starts with the step.

step-effect.duration.description: How long the effect lasts in seconds. The step lasts at least until the effect ends.

color.description: The stop's color. It is a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color is along the gradient from 0 to 1. A stop whose `position` is less than an earlier stop's is placed where the previous stop is.

tail.x.description: How far across the frame in fractions of its width.

tail.y.description: How far down the frame in fractions of its height.

depth.description: How far the letters are extruded in ems. The bevels on the front and the back add `bevel` each. The letters' fronts are then `depth` + 2 × `bevel` from the slide. The default is 0.2.

bevel.description: How far the letters' edges are rounded in ems. At 0, they are sharp. The default is 0.02.

file.description: The path to the model a program built from the words. It is a GLB's path relative to the presentation's folder.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the GLB was built from. It is written as `markdownpoint/text-model/<rule>:sha256:<hex>`. With 22 as its `<rule>`, it ends with the SHA-256 of a record of the text's words, the values of the fields they show, the presentation's `locale`, the family of each font role the words use and all the theme's files for that family, and the text's style and layout. The record is written according to RFC 8785's JSON Canonicalization Scheme. A reader that doesn't know the rule draws the text flat.

tilt.x.description: How many degrees the object turns about the horizontal axis. With a positive x, its top turns away from the viewer. CSS's `rotateX()` turns the same way. A 3D object's `rotation.x` turns the other way.

tilt.y.description: How many degrees the object turns about the vertical axis. With a positive y, its left side comes forward. The object's rotation comes first, then the y turn, then the x turn.

start.description: How many seconds into the file or the Action the part that plays starts. The default is 0.

end.description: How many seconds into the file or the Action the part that plays ends. `end` must come after `start`. Without an `end`, the file or the Action plays to its end.

match.description: How `carry-over` matches a text that both slides show with the same id. A text with the same words on both slides moves whole. Its words are compared as shown before `case` changes them, and their markup doesn't count. A line break counts as a space. The break between two paragraphs, headings, or list items counts as a space too. Between two Chinese or Japanese characters, a break doesn't count. On a path, it does. With `object`, a text whose words changed cross-dissolves. With `word` or `character`, a text whose words changed morphs word by word or character by character. A text on a path or with a 3D model on either slide then moves whole, and its old words cross-dissolve into its new ones. The three values of `match` are those of Keynote's Magic Move. The default is `object`.

color.description: The color that `fade-through-color` fades through. It is a color role or a hex color without alpha, such as "#000000". A role's color comes from the scheme of the slide the transition leaves. A role's alpha is ignored. The default is `#000000`.

transition.delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits once the transition into the slide and the slide's last step have ended. It is in seconds. A transition can have a `delay` only with `start: automatically`. Keynote's Delay works the same way. The default is 0.

transition.direction.description: Which way a push, scroll, move in, reveal, or wipe travels across the screen. The default is `left`.

transition.duration.description: How many seconds the transition takes. It's left out when the type is `none`.

transition.interpolation.description: How the transition speeds up and slows down. Only `carry-over` and `scroll` have it. The default is `ease-in-out`.

transition.start.description: Whether the transition starts on a click, or by itself after the slide's last step. Keynote's Start Transition Automatically works the same way. The default is `on-click`.

start.description: Where the drawn part starts along the stroke in fractions of its length.

end.description: Where the drawn part ends along the stroke in fractions of its length.

progress.description: How far the edge has crossed the object's box along `angle`. At 0, the edge is where the box begins. At 1, the soft edge is past the box's far side. A text's box includes the words that run past it. The default is 1.

angle.description: Which way the edge travels in degrees clockwise from up. It is measured in the object's own axes. It turns and scales with the object and its groups, and a flip doesn't mirror it. The default is 90.

feather.description: How wide the soft edge is. It is in canvas units along the object's own axes and scales with the object. Across the soft edge, the object fades from shown to hidden. The default is 0.
